title: Inference Sell Lab — Sketchbook & Ops Notes v1
summary: Working sketch for a compact, demo-forward sales enablement mini-deck + annotated ops notes focused on pilot acceleration, technical handoff, and fast fallback economics. Rough speaker notes and tactical scripts included for SEs and field ops. Intentionally informal — meant to be iterated in SE working session.
content:
Context and intent:
- Problem: SEs need a >5 minute demo + 1 pager that answers: "Is the inference fast enough? Will it be predictable/cost-stable? What happens if traffic spikes?"
- Goal: produce a micro-deck + ops checklist that helps convert pilots to reserved capacity or Dedicated trials. Emphasize lightweight proofs (embed/cache pilot, controlled traffic ramp, traceable SLOs).
- Audience: SEs, platform buyers, integration architects.

High-level deck outline (6 slides, tiny):
1) One-liner + value (30s)
   - Title slide: "Make inference predictable: latency, cost, and fallback in minutes"
   - Quick verbal hook: "We'll show a 5-min demo + plan to keep your app online if load spikes. No deep infra changes."
   - Speaker cue: call out model, route, and region up front (helps with procurement/security).

2) Demo premise + success metric (30s)
   - Bullet: "Demo: chat endpoint, 2 routes: low-latency vs cost-optimized. Metric: p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens."
   - Quick note: show Console route-level breakdown during demo (latency/cost heatmap).

3) Live demo script (2–3 min) — exact steps for SE
   - Prep: set demo account = sample app on hosted API; ensure routing policy points to a 'canary' model variant.
   - Step 1: Run single short request (show p50/p95 in Console). Say: "p95 ~120ms for 512 tokens (example)" — use placeholder numbers and adapt per customer.
   - Step 2: Toggle to cost-optimized route (quantized variant). Show response time increases, cost drop.
   - Step 3: Trigger a synthetic small burst (local script or Console load tool), show fallback to cheaper region/model when load crosses threshold.
   - Notes: have a saved Console view and 1 slide with the three clicks.

4) Fast pilot scope + guardrails (1 slide)
   - Pilot window: 2–4 weeks, daytime traffic only, limited token budget (e.g., 5M tokens/week)
   - Acceptance criteria: p95 < target, error rate < 1%, cost per unit within budget
   - Ops guardrails: route-based rate limits, circuit-breaker pattern, automatic model fallback configured in 10 minutes.

5) Fallback economics + decision map (1 slide)
   - Visual (sketch): if latency > SLO and capacity constrained -> route to cheaper quantized variant -> if still saturated -> region fallthrough to Dedicated reserve or cached responses.
   - Quick script for sellers: "If they care about uptime, we prioritize model fallback + cache; if they care about quality, lock to hosted with reserved Dedicated commit."

6) Next steps and handoff checklist (1 slide)
   - SE checklist items: set up demo tenant, attach audit logs, create a canary route, prepare 3 prompt variations for quality checks, agree on pilot KPIs and escalation path.

Speaker notes + rough lines for SEs (copyable)
- Opening 15s: "We built Redwood Inference to let teams ship LLM features without guessing about cost or uptime. In five minutes I'll show how we can prove that for your workload."
- On latency vs cost tradeoff: "We can tune batching, cache TTLs, or select quantized model variants — all configurable per route so you don't change your app code."
- Handling objections (short):
  - "What if outputs regress?" -> "We run baseline evals on your prompt set, and can route specific prompts to higher-fidelity variants until you're ready to commit."
  - "What about PII/compliance?" -> "Private deployment option with customer-managed VPC and KMS; audit logs visible in Console."
  - "How do we avoid surprise charges?" -> "We cap token usage per route and have reserved capacity options for predictable pricing."

Ops-ready pilot handoff (practical steps)
- Pre-demo prep (day -2): create demo tenant, generate API key with read-only Console, upload 3 canonical prompts, and attach a simple dashboard link.
- Day 0: run demo script. Invite platform architect and SRE.
- Day 1–7: controlled traffic ramp (50k tokens/day -> 200k/day), monitor p95 and cost per token.
- Week 2: review quality metrics on prompt set; propose either Dedicated reservation or extended hosted trial.

Sample script for fallback rules (non-technical seller phrasing)
- "If requests exceed SLO, Redwood will start routing older cached prefixes and cheaper model variants — this keeps the app responsive while we trigger a capacity expansion or reserved commit. We can show logs for every failover in Console."

Quick triage checklist for SE during pilot (short bullets)
- Are p95 and error rates within agreed thresholds? (Y/N)
- Any prompt-level quality regressions? If yes: route those prompts to fidelity variant.
- Are token consumption patterns steady or spiky? If spiky: enable burst capacity + apply rate limit.
- Do we have audit logs and KMS configured if asked?

Open questions to resolve in SE working session (TODOs)
- Standardize demo placeholder numbers and ranges by model family (LLM-1: p95 80–200ms vs LLM-2: 200–600ms) — need bench data from Applied ML. (assigned: Rina)
- One-click Console saved view for demo (Evan to prototype)
- Short video recording (60s) of the demo for asynchronous prospects (Priya to script)
- Pack a short troubleshooting playbook for common pilot issues (Benji)

Notes to self / iteration log (raw):
- 2025-01-12 initial sketch created (Marcus)
- 2025-01-20 added pilot ramp and triage bullets after SE sync
- 2025-02-03 updated linked artifacts + added TODO ownership

Quick appendix (if SE wants backup slides) — tiny bullets that can be appended to deck:
- Tech proof points: continuous batching, KV cache, route-level quantization, and model pinning.
- Compliance: VPC + HSM/KMS, audit logs, SOC2 mention.
- Pricing hooks: hosted per-token + dedicated reserved commit tradeoffs; show example math for a 100M token month.

End of sketch.

Slack notes / cross-ref: copy this into #se-sprint-ops before next SE sync; attach Confluence page INF-SellLab-2025 for finalization.

-- Marcus
